bottom_line: In patients with atrial fibrillation and a recent acute coronary syndrome or PCI treated with a P2Y12 inhibitor, apixaban resulted in less major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding than a vitamin K antagonist (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.81).
implications: These data support the conclusion that, over 6 months in this trial population, apixaban (vs vitamin K antagonist) reduced ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (10.5% vs. 14.7%; hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.81) and reduced death or hospitalization (23.5% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.93), while death or ischemic event was not significantly different (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.75–1.16). Aspirin (vs placebo) increased bleeding (16.1% vs. 9.0%; hazard ratio, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.59 to 2.24) and did not significantly change death or hospitalization (hazard ratio, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.21). The document notes the trial was not designed to detect small differences in less common individual ischemic outcomes.

major_points.text: International two-by-two factorial randomized trial comparing apixaban vs vitamin K antagonist and aspirin vs placebo for 6 months on a P2Y12 inhibitor background.
major_points.quote: In an international trial with a two-by-two factorial design, we randomly assigned patients... to receive apixaban or a vitamin K antagonist and to receive aspirin or matching placebo for 6 months.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

major_points.text: Major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding occurred more often with aspirin than with placebo.
major_points.quote: and in 16.1% of the patients receiving aspi- rin, as compared with 9.0% of those receiving placebo (hazard ratio, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.59 to 2.24; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Death or hospitalization was lower with apixaban than with vitamin K antagonist, with similar ischemic events.
major_points.quote: Patients in the apixaban group had a lower incidence of death or hospitalization than those in the vitamin K antagonist group (23.5% vs. 27.4%; hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.74 to 0.93; P = 0.002) and a similar incidence of isch- emic events.

criticisms.text: Time in therapeutic range for vitamin K antagonist was modestly lower than in some previous randomized trials.
criticisms.quote: There are limitations to our trial. The time in the therapeutic range for the patients who received a vitamin K antagonist was modestly lower than in some previous randomized trials of stroke preven- tion involving patients with atrial fibrillation.

criticisms.text: Trial not designed to be large enough to detect differences in less common individual ischemic outcomes.
criticisms.quote: Our trial was not designed to be large enough to detect potentially clinically im- portant differences in less common but impor- tant individual ischemic outcomes.

criticisms.text: Many patients probably received aspirin during the pre-randomization period when treatment decisions were at clinician discretion.
criticisms.quote: The mean time from the index event to random- ization was 6.6 days; treatment decisions during this time were left to the discretion of the treating physician, and many patients probably received as- pirin during this time.
